title: Per-Item Caps and the Aggregate Term Limit — Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts
content:
**Article 1 — Item caps.** Each covered item on a Homeowner Service Contract has a per-term cap equal to the tier's limit for that item on the schedule of benefits:

| Covered item | Cap used |
|---|---|
| heating system, cooling system, heating and cooling ductwork | the tier's heating system, cooling system and ductwork limits |
| interior plumbing leak, interior drain stoppage, water heater | the tier's plumbing leak, drain stoppage and water heater limits |
| interior electrical system, ceiling fan, garbage disposal, whirlpool bathtub | the tier's electrical, ceiling fan, garbage disposal and whirlpool bathtub limits |
| refrigerator, oven range and cooktop, dishwasher, built-in microwave | the tier's refrigerator, oven range and cooktop, dishwasher and built-in microwave limits |
| clothes washer, clothes dryer, garage door opener | the tier's clothes washer, clothes dryer and garage door opener limits |

**Article 2 — What counts against the caps (term rule).**

> (2.1) The cap is shared by every repair, replacement, cash-in-lieu settlement and out-of-network reimbursement for that item in the term: the payments on that item on the contract whose service requests fall in the term, less reversals of those authorizations.
>
> (2.2) Every payment on the contract, supplemental allowances included, counts toward the aggregate term limit: every repair, replacement, supplemental allowance, cash-in-lieu and out-of-network payment whose service request falls in the term, less reversals of those authorizations.
>
> (2.3) A payment counts in the term in which its service request's request date falls, even when authorized after a renewal.
>
> (2.4) The remaining item benefit is the item cap less the item's payments counted under 2.1, and the remaining aggregate benefit is the aggregate term limit less the payments counted under 2.2, each floored at zero.

**Retirement notice for Article 2.** Clauses 2.1 to 2.4 are no longer in force for the payments listed below; those payments are measured under the current rules that govern them. For every other payment the term rule in clauses 2.1 to 2.4 remains in force.

| Payment | Clauses no longer in force for it |
|---|---|
| a replacement authorized after a stalled repair | 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4 |
| a customer-elected cash settlement | 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4 |
| a company-elected cash offer made because no network contractor can install the like unit | 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4 |
| the payment on acceptance of such a company-elected offer | 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4 |
| a haul-away allowance on a Bridgewell replacement whose completion report is on file | 2.2, 2.3, 2.4 |

**Article 3 — Clauses in force for every payment.** The cap that applies is the one of the tier under which the request is determined; when an upgrade raised an item's cap, payments made before the upgrade in the same term still count against it. A reversed authorization stops counting from its reversal. When either the remaining item benefit or the remaining aggregate benefit is zero, nothing further is paid for that item in the term. Supplemental allowances count toward the aggregate limit but not toward any item cap. Service call fees never count toward any cap and never reduce one.

**Illustration under the term rule (hypothetical figures).** A Bridgewell HomeCare Silver contract, whose schedule of benefits sets the water heater limit at 1500.00 and the aggregate term limit at 15000.00, has 1,200.00 already counted on the water heater this term and 14,000.00 counted across the contract this term, allowances included. The remaining item benefit is 300.00 and the remaining aggregate benefit is 1,000.00. A service call fee collected on the request changes neither figure.
